children.why_this_cut: The first child covers the section intro and the 'Try to prevent imminent real-world harm' subsection (L1414-1541), ending at the close of the knife-handling example. The only linkage crossing the cut is the 'prevent_imminent_harm' principle, which is established in this child and used by the section as a whole; it is seeded below.

The second child covers the 'Do not facilitate or encourage illicit behavior' and 'Do not encourage self-harm, delusions, or mania' subsections (L1543-1706), plus the blank line at L1542. The only cross-cutting linkage is the 'do_not_facilitate_illicit_behavior' and 'do_not_encourage_self_harm' principles, both established within this child and seeded below.

The third child covers the 'Provide information without giving regulated advice' and 'Support users in mental health discussions' subsections (L1708-1797), plus the blank line at L1707. The only cross-cutting linkage is the 'avoid_regulated_advice' and 'support_mental_health' principles, both established within this child and seeded below.

expected_cross_links.evidence: The 'prevent_imminent_harm' principle is established in child 1 (L1418-1420) and is the governing principle for the entire risky_situations section; child 2 and child 3's subsections are all part of the same section and may reference it.
expected_cross_links.name: prevent_imminent_harm

expected_cross_links.name: support_mental_health

judgment_calls: Could have cut at L1541 instead of L1542; chose L1542 because the blank line at L1542 belongs to the earlier child and the 'Do not facilitate' subsection starts cleanly at L1543. A cut at L1541 would have left the blank line dangling.

Could have cut at L1706 instead of L1707; chose L1707 because the blank line at L1707 belongs to the earlier child and the 'Provide information' subsection starts cleanly at L1708. A cut at L1706 would have left the blank line dangling.
The three children are roughly equal in size (128, 165, 91 lines respectively); the cut at L1542 and L1707 are the only clean boundaries between subsections, so the uneven split is justified.

seed_vocabulary.name: prevent_imminent_harm
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle of proactively trying to prevent imminent real-world harm when the assistant identifies a dangerous situation, while avoiding overstepping or being judgmental

seed_vocabulary.name: do_not_facilitate_illicit_behavior
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle of refusing to help facilitate illicit behavior, including guidance, instructions, actionable steps, or improvements to user-provided plans

seed_vocabulary.name: do_not_encourage_self_harm
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle of not encouraging or enabling self-harm, and responding supportively when context suggests a credible risk to the user's safety or life

seed_vocabulary.name: avoid_regulated_advice
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle of equipping the user with information without providing definitive advice on sensitive or important topics (legal, medical, financial) that would be best given by a licensed professional

seed_vocabulary.name: support_mental_health
seed_vocabulary.prose: the principle of creating a supportive, empathetic, and understanding environment for mental health topics, without judgment or dismissiveness

seed_vocabulary.name: risky_situations
seed_vocabulary.prose: the section providing instructions for handling requests that involve risky situations

seed_vocabulary.name: root_level_rule
seed_vocabulary.prose: a fundamental root rule that cannot be overridden by system messages, developers or users

seed_vocabulary.name: developer_level_rule
seed_vocabulary.prose: an instruction given by developers using the API, which models should obey unless overridden by root or system instructions

seed_vocabulary.name: user_level_rule
seed_vocabulary.prose: an instruction from end users, which models should honor unless they conflict with developer-, system-, or root-level instructions
